key_insight: BAR helps an LLM reason over medical knowledge graphs under a fixed budget by planning, retrieving, and verifying cited evidence instead of using the graph as a static lookup source.
clinical_relevance: This could improve post-discharge risk prediction by making model outputs more traceable to specific medical knowledge and easier to review retrospectively.
method: Builds disease-specific evidence graphs with support scores and provenance.
Uses an LLM plan-navigate-verify loop to retrieve evidence within a patient budget and revise when verification fails.
Trains a policy with rewards for predictive gain, lower acquisition cost, and citation integrity.
evidence_signal: Across 8 diseases and 3 prediction horizons on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, BAR improved AUPRC by 3.4 points, raised citation precision from 59.8% to 77.9%, and used only 62-65% of the budget cap.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of KG provenance and the citation pipeline, so poor evidence annotation or shifting clinical settings could reduce reliability.
paper_title: Cite What You Explore: Budget-Aware LLM Reasoning over Medical KGs with Verifiable Evidence
